intent.raw_query: Morocco Marrakech and Sahara, $1000 solo, 7 days, March 2026

selected_hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Djemaa el-Fna Square & Medina Exploration
experiences.description: Immerse yourself in the beating heart of Marrakech by wandering the ancient medina souks and witnessing the nightly spectacle of Djemaa el-Fna square, filled with storytellers, snake charmers, musicians, and food stalls. Hire a local guide for deeper historical context on the UNESCO-listed medina.

experiences.name: Overnight Sahara Desert Camel Trek & Bivouac Camp
experiences.description: Ride camels at sunset into the golden Erg Chebbi dunes near Merzouga, spend the night in a traditional Berber desert camp under a canopy of stars, enjoy live Gnawa music around a campfire, and wake up for a breathtaking sunrise over the dunes before trekking back.
experiences.location: Erg Chebbi Dunes, Merzouga, Sahara Desert

experiences.name: Bahia Palace & Saadian Tombs Historical Tour
experiences.description: Explore two of Marrakech's most significant historical landmarks: the opulent 19th-century Bahia Palace with its intricate Moroccan tilework and carved cedarwood ceilings, followed by the Saadian Tombs, a stunning 16th-century royal necropolis hidden for centuries and rediscovered in 1917.

experiences.name: Traditional Moroccan Cooking Class in a Riad
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class hosted inside a beautifully restored riad in the medina. Visit the local spice market with your chef, then learn to prepare classic dishes such as lamb tagine, bastilla, and harira soup using authentic Berber spices and techniques passed down through generations.

experiences.name: Todra Gorge Hike & Draa Valley Drive
experiences.description: En route between Marrakech and the Sahara, stop at the dramatic Todra Gorge — towering 300-meter canyon walls carved by the Todra River — for a scenic hike along the canyon floor. Continue through the lush Draa Valley, passing ancient kasbahs, palm oases, and traditional Berber villages.
experiences.location: Todra Gorge, Tinghir Province, Southern Morocco

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Take a petit taxi (negotiate fare, ~50-70 MAD) or shared transfer to your riad in Djemaa el-Fna, Medina. Check in, freshen up, and get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: First walk through Djemaa el-Fna square and the surrounding souks. Explore the labyrinthine alleyways of the Medina at your own pace — browse spice stalls, leather goods, and Berber carpets. Visit the free exterior of the Koutoubia Mosque (the largest mosque in Marrakech) just a short walk from the square.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Djemaa el-Fna at sunset to witness the square transform into a massive open-air spectacle — snake charmers, storytellers, acrobats, and food stalls. Grab a seat at one of the rooftop cafés overlooking the square for mint tea and the view.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack at the airport or skip — arrival is at 13:00.
meals.lunch: Street food at Djemaa el-Fna square: harira soup (5 MAD), msemen flatbread (3 MAD), or a fresh-squeezed orange juice (4 MAD). Budget: ~15-25 MAD.
meals.dinner: Eat at one of the famous food stalls (numbered 1–100) in Djemaa el-Fna. Try lamb or chicken tagine, kefta skewers, and Moroccan salad. Budget: ~40-60 MAD per person.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some euros or dollars to Moroccan Dirhams (MAD) at the airport or a bureau de change in the Medina. Avoid unlicensed money changers. Keep small bills handy for street food and tips. Arrival day — keep it light and relaxed.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Bahia Palace (entrance ~10 MAD) — a stunning 19th-century palace with intricate tilework, painted ceilings, and lush gardens. Arrive early (opens 9:00) to beat crowds. Afterward, walk through the Mellah (Jewish Quarter) nearby to see its distinctive architecture and covered market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Saadian Tombs (entrance ~70 MAD) — beautifully decorated royal tombs dating from the 16th century. Then explore the El Badi Palace ruins (entrance ~70 MAD), a once-magnificent palace now partially standing but atmospheric. Both are within walking distance of each other in the southern Medina.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll through the Rue des Épices (Spice Square) area in the northern souks. Visit the Medersa Ben Youssef (entrance ~70 MAD, check closing time) — a 14th-century Islamic college with breathtaking Moorish architecture. End the evening back at Djemaa el-Fna for dinner.

meals.breakfast: At your riad (if included) or a local café near the Medina: msemen with honey and argan oil, mint tea. Budget: ~20-30 MAD.
meals.lunch: Sandwich shop near the Mellah or a local snack stall: merguez sandwich or kefta wrap. Budget: ~15-25 MAD.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Chez Bahia or similar local eatery near the Medina: chicken tagine with olives and preserved lemon, Moroccan bread. Budget: ~50-80 MAD.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — the Medina streets are uneven cobblestone. Entrance fees for Bahia Palace, Saadian Tombs, El Badi Palace, and Ben Youssef Medersa can be bundled as a day of sightseeing (~220 MAD total). Dress modestly when entering religious or historical sites.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Ourika Valley (~30 km from Marrakech). Take a shared grand taxi from Bab Rob taxi stand (~20-30 MAD per seat each way). Hike along the Ourika River through Berber villages, terraced fields, and Atlas Mountain foothills. Visit a local Berber family home for tea if invited — a genuine cultural exchange.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue up the valley toward the Setti Fatma waterfalls (7 cascades). The hike to the first waterfall is easy (~20 min), higher ones require more effort. Enjoy the mountain scenery and fresh air. Return to Marrakech by shared taxi in the late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax and recover at the riad. Explore the quieter evening souks near your accommodation — look for handmade lanterns, ceramics, and leather babouche slippers. Enjoy a slow evening dinner.

meals.breakfast: At your riad or local café: khobz bread with olive oil and amlou (almond-argan paste), mint tea. Budget: ~20-30 MAD.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a simple Berber restaurant in Setti Fatma village: tajine of vegetables or lamb, fresh bread, mint tea. Budget: ~50-70 MAD.
meals.dinner: Back in Marrakech — try Café de France or a local Medina restaurant near Djemaa el-Fna: harira soup, couscous, and a glass of avocado smoothie. Budget: ~50-70 MAD.

day_by_day.notes: Bring water, sunscreen, and a light jacket — mountain temperatures can be cooler than the city. Negotiate the grand taxi fare before departing. The Ourika Valley is beautiful in March with green landscapes and possible snow on higher Atlas peaks.

day_by_day.morning: Depart early (6:00-7:00 AM) for the Sahara Desert via a budget shared group tour or CTM/Supratours bus toward Ouarzazate and Merzouga. Book a shared 3-day/2-night Sahara tour in advance (~800-1200 MAD per person all-inclusive) from a reputable agency in the Medina. Travel southeast through the High Atlas Mountains via the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260 m).
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop in Aït Benhaddou — a UNESCO World Heritage ksar (fortified village) used as a film set for Gladiator, Game of Thrones, and Lawrence of Arabia. Explore the ancient mud-brick citadel (~10 MAD entry or free to wander lower sections). Continue driving through the Valley of Roses and Draa Valley palm groves.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in the town of Boumalne Dades or a small guesthouse near the Dades Gorge for overnight stay (included in tour package). Enjoy a communal dinner and rest for the long journey ahead.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at riad before departure or packed snacks for the road. Budget: ~20-30 MAD.
meals.lunch: Roadside restaurant near Aït Benhaddou: tagine and salad, bread, mint tea. Budget: ~50-70 MAD (often included in tour).
meals.dinner: Included in guesthouse/tour package: Moroccan couscous or tagine, harira, Moroccan salad. Budget: included in tour.

day_by_day.notes: Book your Sahara tour 1-2 days in advance from your riad or a trusted Medina agency. Compare prices — a 3-day shared tour should cost ~800-1200 MAD and include transport, accommodation, camel trek, and most meals. Bring warm layers — desert nights are cold in March (can drop to 5°C).

day_by_day.morning: Continue driving toward Merzouga and the Erg Chebbi dunes — the iconic Saharan dune sea reaching up to 150 m high. Pass through the Todra Gorge (a stunning 300 m high canyon) for a short walk along the river at the base of the gorge. A spectacular natural landmark and popular with rock climbers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at a desert camp near Merzouga. Check into a basic Berber desert camp (included in tour). Rest, explore the edge of the dunes on foot, and watch the shifting colors of the sand in the afternoon light. Optional: quad biking on the dunes (~150-200 MAD for 30 min, paid separately).
day_by_day.evening: Mount camels for a 1-hour sunset camel trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes (included in tour). Arrive at a traditional nomad-style camp deep in the dunes. Watch the Saharan sunset paint the dunes gold and red. Enjoy a campfire, Berber music, drumming, and stargazing under one of the darkest skies in Africa. Overnight in a desert camp tent.

meals.breakfast: Included at guesthouse: bread, olive oil, honey, argan jam, mint tea.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch or simple tagine near Todra Gorge: ~50 MAD (sometimes included in tour).
meals.dinner: Included at desert camp: traditional Berber meal — tagine, couscous, Moroccan salad, mint tea, dates around the campfire.

day_by_day.notes: Bring a headlamp, warm sleeping layers, and a scarf or shemagh for sand. The desert nights in March can be very cold — temperatures drop sharply after sunset. The Milky Way is stunningly visible from the Sahara on clear nights. Protect your camera and phone from sand.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (around 6:00 AM) to climb a high dune and watch the Saharan sunrise — one of the most memorable experiences of the trip. Return to camp for breakfast. Begin the long drive back toward Marrakech, taking a different southern route through the Draa Valley and Zagora.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop in the Draa Valley — a lush 200 km palm grove oasis stretching along the Draa River. Visit a small kasbah or local market in Zagora. Continue driving northwest through the Anti-Atlas foothills and desert plains. Stop at a fossil market near Erfoud (the region is famous for ancient trilobite and ammonite fossils — great cheap souvenirs at ~20-50 MAD).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech late evening (~21:00-22:00 depending on route). Check back into your riad. Grab a light late-night snack from Djemaa el-Fna stalls (open until midnight) and rest.

meals.breakfast: Included at desert camp: Moroccan bread, olive oil, honey, mint tea, hard-boiled eggs.
meals.lunch: Roadside stop in Zagora or Draa Valley: tagine or sandwich, mint tea. Budget: ~40-60 MAD (sometimes included in tour).
meals.dinner: Late-night street food at Djemaa el-Fna: harira soup, kefta sandwich, or a bowl of snail soup (traditional). Budget: ~30-50 MAD.

day_by_day.notes: The return drive is long (~8-9 hours with stops). Sleep in the car when possible. Bring snacks and water for the journey. The fossil souvenirs near Erfoud make excellent lightweight budget gifts — bargain hard, starting at 50% of the asking price.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — visit the Majorelle Garden (entrance ~70 MAD, or just admire the blue walls from outside to save money). If budget allows, the Yves Saint Laurent Museum is adjacent (~80 MAD). Alternatively, spend the morning doing last-minute souvenir shopping in the souks: argan oil, spices, leather goods, Berber jewelry, hand-painted ceramics.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Musée de Marrakech (entrance ~50 MAD) in the northern Medina — housed in a beautiful 19th-century palace with rotating art exhibitions and a stunning central courtyard. Grab lunch nearby and do a final walk through the Mouassine neighborhood — one of the Medina's most photogenic quarters with a 16th-century fountain and artisan workshops.
day_by_day.evening: Final sunset from a rooftop café overlooking Djemaa el-Fna — try Café Argana or Le Grand Balcon du Café Glacier for the classic view. Enjoy a farewell Moroccan dinner in the square or a nearby restaurant. Pack your bags for departure.

meals.breakfast: At your riad (if included) or a local café: beghrir (Moroccan pancakes with honey and butter), mint tea. Budget: ~20-30 MAD.
meals.lunch: Souk lunch near Mouassine: fresh-pressed orange juice, msemen, and a bowl of harira. Budget: ~25-35 MAD.
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a mid-range Medina restaurant: pastilla (sweet pigeon or chicken pie), lamb tagine with prunes and almonds, mint tea and pastries. Budget: ~80-120 MAD — a slight splurge for the final night.

day_by_day.notes: Check out time at your riad is typically 11:00-12:00. Ask to store luggage if your departure flight is later. Marrakech Menara Airport is only 5-6 km from the Medina — a petit taxi should cost ~60-80 MAD. Allow 2 hours before your flight for check-in. A 7-day total estimated budget (excluding flights): ~2,500-3,500 MAD (~$250-350 USD) per person including accommodation, food, transport, and activities.

trip_options.title: Classic Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Transfer to your boutique riad in the Medina (~30 min by taxi, ~150 MAD). Check in, freshen up, and settle into your accommodation near Djemaa el-Fna.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle first exploration of Djemaa el-Fna square and its immediate surroundings. Wander through the northern edge of the souks (Souk Semmarine) to get your bearings without overwhelming yourself. Visit the nearby Koutoubia Mosque gardens for a relaxed introduction to Marrakech's iconic skyline — the minaret is visible from almost everywhere.
day_by_day.evening: Experience the magical transformation of Djemaa el-Fna at dusk: snake charmers, storytellers, musicians, and dozens of food stalls ignite the square. Climb to a rooftop café terrace (Café de France or Café Argana) for a panoramic view over the square with a mint tea in hand. Then dive into the night market atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Snack on the plane or grab a light pastry and coffee at a café near the riad upon arrival
meals.lunch: Street food at Djemaa el-Fna square: freshly squeezed orange juice (4 MAD), msemen flatbread with honey, and a bowl of harira soup from a local stall (~40–60 MAD total)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Jardin (Mouassine district, 10-min walk) — a beautifully restored riad restaurant with a lush courtyard. Try the lamb tagine with prunes and almonds. Mid-range: ~150–200 MAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light — jet lag and travel fatigue are real. Exchange currency at the airport or a bureau de change in the Medina (avoid hotel rates). Carry small change for street food. Dress modestly when entering the Medina area out of respect for local customs.

day_by_day.morning: Full immersion in Marrakech's historic monuments. Start at the Bahia Palace (9:00 AM, ~70 MAD entry) — a stunning 19th-century vizier's palace with intricate zellij tilework, carved cedarwood ceilings, and lush gardens. Then walk 10 minutes to the Saadian Tombs (9:30–10:30 AM, ~70 MAD) — a hidden necropolis rediscovered in 1917, housing ornately decorated royal mausoleums from the 16th century.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the Ben Youssef Madrasa (closed for renovation — check status; if open ~70 MAD), one of North Africa's largest historic Quranic schools with breathtaking Andalusian-Moroccan architecture. Afterward, explore the adjacent Musée de Marrakech (~50 MAD) housed in a 19th-century palace. Spend the late afternoon getting wonderfully lost in the labyrinthine souks — Souk des Teinturiers (dyers' souk) and Souk des Épices (spice market) are highlights.
day_by_day.evening: Visit Dar Cherifa, a beautifully restored 16th-century riad turned cultural space and café, for evening mint tea and live Gnawa music (if scheduled). Return to Djemaa el-Fna for a final evening stroll.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your riad (typically included): msemen, amlou (argan oil and almond paste), fresh orange juice, and coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad Restaurant (near Rahba Kedima square) — modern Moroccan cuisine with rooftop views. Try the kefta cigars or vegetable couscous. ~120–160 MAD per person
meals.dinner: Dinner at Chez Lamine Hadj Mustapha near Djemaa el-Fna — a legendary spot for mechoui (slow-roasted lamb). Sold by weight, incredibly authentic. ~100–140 MAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes — cobblestone streets are uneven. Hire a licensed guide from the official tourism office (~300 MAD for a half-day) if you'd like expert context on the monuments. Bargaining in the souks is expected — start at 40–50% of the asking price and enjoy the process.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to the Ourika Valley and Atlas Mountains (~30 km south of Marrakech, 45-min drive). Hire a shared taxi or join a small group tour (~200–300 MAD per person round trip). Hike to the beautiful Setti Fatma waterfalls — a series of seven cascades. The first waterfall is an easy 20-minute walk; the upper falls require a moderate 1-hour scramble with local guides (~50 MAD tip). Stunning Atlas scenery with Berber villages along the way.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop at a Berber family home in the valley for a traditional lunch. On the return to Marrakech, visit the Anima Garden (André Heller's surrealist art garden, ~120 MAD) or the Jardin Majorelle (Yves Saint Laurent's famous blue garden, ~150 MAD + Berber Museum ~30 MAD) — a peaceful oasis of cacti, cobalt blue buildings, and exotic plants.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening back in Marrakech. Browse the lantern and leather goods shops in the Mellah (historic Jewish quarter) near Djemaa el-Fna. Enjoy a hammam experience at a mid-range local hammam (Hammam Dar el-Bacha, ~250 MAD for traditional scrub and steam) to soothe tired muscles.

meals.breakfast: Riad breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Traditional Berber lunch in Ourika Valley — tagine, salads, and bread cooked over charcoal in a local family guesthouse (~80–120 MAD per person)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Terrasse des Épices (Souk Cherifa rooftop) — relaxed atmosphere, Moroccan-fusion menu, great views. ~150–180 MAD per person

day_by_day.notes: Book the Ourika Valley taxi the night before from your riad reception. Bring a light jacket — the Atlas foothills can be cooler even in March. The waterfall hike involves river crossings on stepping stones; wear waterproof shoes or sandals. Jardin Majorelle gets crowded — arrive by 4:00 PM for a quieter experience.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (7:00 AM) for the Sahara Desert — a scenic 8–9 hour drive to Merzouga via the Draa Valley and Todra Gorge. Travel by private or shared transfer (~600–900 MAD per person for a shared minibus tour; ~1,800–2,500 MAD for a private vehicle). Pass through Aït Benhaddou (UNESCO World Heritage ksar) — stop for 1.5 hours to explore this ancient fortified village used as a backdrop for Game of Thrones and Gladiator.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the dramatic Draa Valley — palm groves, kasbahs, and oasis villages. Stop at the Skoura Oasis for a brief walk through the palmery. Arrive in the Dades Valley or Tinghir by late afternoon. Optional: short walk into the lower section of Todra Gorge — towering 300-meter limestone canyon walls, incredibly dramatic.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive at your desert camp or guesthouse near Merzouga (Erg Chebbi dunes) by 7:00–8:00 PM. Check in to a mid-range desert camp (e.g., Kasbah Mohayut or similar — pre-book, ~400–600 MAD per person including dinner and breakfast). Watch the stars emerge over the Sahara — zero light pollution makes this extraordinary.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the riad before departure (request it the night before)
meals.lunch: Roadside lunch stop in Ouarzazate or near Aït Benhaddou — a local restaurant serving tagine and Moroccan salads. ~80–100 MAD per person
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber dinner at the desert camp — harira soup, tagine, couscous, and mint tea served around a fire. Typically included in camp package

day_by_day.notes: This is a long travel day — bring snacks, water, and entertainment. The road over the Tizi n'Tichka pass (2,260 m) can be cold in March — dress in layers. Book your desert camp well in advance as good mid-range options fill up. Confirm the transfer includes stops at Aït Benhaddou and Todra Gorge when booking.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise (5:30 AM) for a camel trek into the Erg Chebbi dunes — the highlight of the trip. Ride by camelback to a dune summit to watch the Sahara sunrise paint the sands in gold and amber. Spend 1–2 hours exploring the dunes on foot — climb the tallest dunes for panoramic views. Optional: quad biking or sandboarding on the dunes (~150–250 MAD extra). Return to camp for a traditional Berber breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the village of Merzouga and the nearby Dayet Srji salt lake (flamingos sometimes present in spring). Explore the Gnawa musicians' quarter in Khamlia village (5 km from Merzouga) — a small community of Sub-Saharan descendants who perform hypnotic Gnawa spiritual music. Attend an informal performance (~50–100 MAD donation). Rest during the hottest part of the day (1:00–3:00 PM) at the camp or guesthouse.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset camel or walk back into the dunes for golden hour photography — the light on Erg Chebbi at sunset is extraordinary. Bonfire evening at the camp with drumming, Berber music, and stargazing. The Sahara sky in March is exceptionally clear.

meals.breakfast: Berber desert breakfast at camp: msemen, argan oil, honey, hard-boiled eggs, mint tea (included in camp package)
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local Merzouga restaurant or the camp: tagine, Moroccan salads, fresh bread. ~80–100 MAD per person
meals.dinner: Second night camp dinner — often a mechoui (whole roasted lamb) or couscous feast for groups. Included in camp package or ~150 MAD supplement

day_by_day.notes: Bring a warm layer for the pre-dawn camel trek — Sahara mornings in March can be 5–10°C. Sunscreen, sunglasses, and a headscarf/shemagh are essential for dune activities. Tip your camel guide (~50–100 MAD). Charge all devices the night before as some camps have limited electricity during the day.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Merzouga by 8:00 AM for the return journey to Marrakech via a different northern route through the Ziz Valley and Midelt. Stop at the Ziz Gorges — a dramatic river canyon cutting through the High Atlas. Visit the town of Er Rachidia briefly. The route through the cedar forests near Azrou offers chances to spot wild Barbary macaque monkeys.
day_by_day.afternoon: Stop in Ifrane — Morocco's 'Little Switzerland,' a charming colonial-era town with European-style architecture at 1,665 m altitude. Continue through Azrou's cedar forest for the macaque encounter (bring nuts to feed them). Arrive in Fès or continue toward Marrakech depending on energy levels. If time allows, a brief stop in Midelt (the 'apple capital' of Morocco) for local produce.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Marrakech by 7:00–8:00 PM (or spend the night in Fès if you prefer — adds a bonus city). Return to your riad, shower off the desert dust, and enjoy a quiet final Marrakech evening strolling Djemaa el-Fna.

meals.breakfast: Final camp breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Lunch stop in Midelt or Azrou — try a local café for a bowl of harira, Moroccan bread, and lamb chops. ~70–100 MAD per person
meals.dinner: Celebratory final dinner at Dar Yacout or a special riad restaurant in Marrakech — a classic Moroccan feast in a candlelit palace setting. ~250–350 MAD per person (splurge-worthy)

day_by_day.notes: The northern return route is longer (10–11 hours) but far more scenic and less traveled than the outbound road. Confirm your return transfer includes these stops. Alternatively, fly Merzouga–Marrakech if available (rare but sometimes chartered). Book the evening dinner in advance — popular riad restaurants require reservations.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — revisit your favorite corner of the Medina at a leisurely pace without the pressure of sightseeing. Browse the Mellah market for last-minute souvenirs: argan oil, saffron, rose water, leather goods, and handwoven textiles. Visit the El Badi Palace ruins (~70 MAD) if not yet seen — a hauntingly beautiful 16th-century palace with storks nesting on the towers.
day_by_day.afternoon: Relax at a rooftop café or the Majorelle Garden (if not visited on Day 3) for a peaceful final afternoon. Pack and prepare for departure. Enjoy a final mint tea ritual at a traditional café — order 'atay' and watch the elaborate pouring ceremony. Transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport (allow 1.5 hours before flight time).
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Marrakech. Carry the scents of spices, the sound of Gnawa drums, and the memory of Sahara stars home with you.

meals.breakfast: Riad breakfast — savor it slowly on your last morning. Try to request a rooftop table if available
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café des Épices (Rahba Kedima square) — a Marrakech institution with simple, fresh Moroccan dishes and great people-watching from the terrace. ~100–130 MAD per person
meals.dinner: Airport or in-flight meal (or an early dinner near the airport if time permits)

day_by_day.notes: Marrakech airport can be busy on Sundays — allow extra time. Duty-free at the airport has decent argan products if you missed shopping. Declare any food items (saffron, spices) at customs if required by your destination country. Keep 200–300 MAD in cash for airport taxi and tips. A 7-day Morocco experience like this typically costs ~4,000–6,000 MAD per person (excluding flights) at mid-range level.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Morocco – Marrakech and Sahara Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Djemaa el-Fna, Medina, Marrakech Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Marrakech Menara Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to your boutique riad in Djemaa el-Fna, Medina. Check-in, freshen up, and enjoy a welcome mint tea ceremony hosted by the riad staff.
day_by_day.afternoon: Gentle orientation walk around Djemaa el-Fna square — absorb the energy of snake charmers, storytellers, and musicians. Stroll into the adjacent Souk Semmarine for a first taste of the medina's labyrinthine lanes. Visit the iconic Koutoubia Mosque gardens (exterior) for a peaceful introduction to Marrakech's architecture.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset aperitif on the rooftop terrace of your riad overlooking the medina skyline. Head to Djemaa el-Fna as the square transforms into a vast open-air theatre — food stalls, acrobats, and Gnawa musicians create an unforgettable atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (arrival day — welcome mint tea and Moroccan pastries provided at riad upon check-in)
meals.lunch: Light meal at the riad or a quick stop at Café de France overlooking Djemaa el-Fna for harira soup and Moroccan flatbread
meals.dinner: Dinner at La Maison Arabe — a legendary Marrakech institution offering refined Moroccan cuisine including bastilla au pigeon, slow-cooked lamb tagine with preserved lemon, and house-made pastilla dessert in an elegant courtyard setting

day_by_day.notes: Flight LH lands at 13:00 — allow approximately 45–60 minutes for immigration, baggage, and private transfer to the medina. Day 1 is intentionally relaxed to allow acclimatisation. Confirm riad check-in time in advance as medina access for vehicles is restricted — a porter will meet you at the nearest accessible point.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of the Bahia Palace — a 19th-century masterpiece of Moroccan craftsmanship featuring intricate zellige tilework, carved cedarwood ceilings, and lush interior gardens. Continue to the Saadian Tombs, a hidden necropolis rediscovered in 1917, housing the ornately decorated royal mausoleum of the Saadian dynasty.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the El Badi Palace ruins — once described as one of the most magnificent palaces in the world, now an evocative ruin housing a museum of Moroccan arts. Afterwards, visit the Museum of Confluences (Dar Si Said) for an exceptional collection of Moroccan decorative arts, Berber jewellery, and ancient textiles.
day_by_day.evening: Private sunset rooftop experience at a premium riad-restaurant in the medina. Followed by a curated Gnawa music performance arranged privately through your riad concierge — an intimate cultural experience with traditional musicians in a courtyard setting.

meals.breakfast: Full Moroccan breakfast at the riad — msemen flatbreads, amlou (argan oil and almond paste), fresh-squeezed orange juice, soft-boiled eggs, local honey, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at Nomad Restaurant — a stylish rooftop eatery near the Spice Square (Rahba Kedima) offering modern Moroccan cuisine with panoramic medina views. Try the lamb mechoui salad and chargrilled vegetable couscous
meals.dinner: Dinner at Le Tobsil — one of Marrakech's most celebrated fine-dining experiences, set within a candlelit riad courtyard. Fixed-menu feast of multiple Moroccan courses including pastilla, tagines, and traditional sweets with live Andalusian music

day_by_day.notes: Book Le Tobsil well in advance as it is highly sought after. Wear comfortable walking shoes for the morning palace tour — cobblestone streets can be uneven. Consider hiring a licensed private guide for the morning to enrich the historical context of both palaces.

day_by_day.morning: Private half-day excursion to the Majorelle Garden — the iconic cobalt-blue botanical sanctuary created by French painter Jacques Majorelle and later restored by Yves Saint Laurent. Visit the adjoining Berber Museum (Musée Berbère) within the garden, housing one of North Africa's finest collections of Amazigh art and artefacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury hammam and spa experience at a premium establishment such as Les Bains de Marrakech or Royal Mansour Spa — enjoy a traditional black soap (beldi) scrub, ghassoul clay mask, and argan oil massage. Return to the medina for a guided private souk experience — your expert guide navigates the souks of the spice market, leather tanneries (Chouara), and artisan cooperatives.
day_by_day.evening: Rooftop cocktail hour at a chic Guéliz bar or the rooftop of Selman Marrakech. Dinner at a premium restaurant before an optional visit to a traditional Moroccan folklore show featuring acrobats, fire dancers, and Berber musicians.

meals.breakfast: Riad breakfast — fresh fruit platter, Moroccan crepes (beghrir), argan oil, local goat cheese, and freshly brewed coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Café Kif Kif or Palais Khum near the Majorelle Garden area — light mezze-style spread with Moroccan salads, grilled brochettes, and fresh juices
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dar Yacout — an iconic Marrakech palace-restaurant with rooftop cocktails, multiple lantern-lit dining rooms, and an elaborate multi-course Moroccan feast; an unmissable theatrical dining experience

day_by_day.notes: Majorelle Garden can be busy mid-morning — aim to arrive at opening time (9:30 AM) for a more serene experience. Book the hammam session in advance. The private souk tour in the afternoon is best arranged through your riad concierge with a trusted guide to avoid tourist traps and ensure authentic artisan visits.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Marrakech early (6:00–7:00 AM) by private luxury 4x4 vehicle for the journey to the Sahara Desert via the dramatic Tizi n'Tichka mountain pass (2,260m elevation) through the High Atlas Mountains. Stop at the UNESCO-listed Aït Benhaddou — a breathtaking ancient ksar (fortified village) that has served as a backdrop for films including Gladiator and Game of Thrones. Private guided tour of the ksar with a local Berber expert.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Drâa Valley — a lush corridor of palm oases, kasbahs, and rose-cultivating villages (the Valley of Roses). Stop at the historic Kasbah Taourirt in Ouarzazate. Continue through the lunar landscapes of the Jebel Saghro range toward Merzouga and the Erg Chebbi dunes. Arrive at your luxury desert camp or premium lodge by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Mount camels (or opt for a 4x4) for a guided sunset ride into the Erg Chebbi dunes — the golden hour light transforms the dunes into a dramatic sea of amber and copper. Arrive at your private luxury desert camp for sundowners on the dunes. Stargazing experience with a local astronomer guide under one of Africa's darkest skies.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the riad before departure — packed premium breakfast box provided for the road if departing before 7:00 AM
meals.lunch: Lunch stop at a quality restaurant in or near Ouarzazate — traditional Berber lamb tagine with prunes and almonds, fresh Moroccan salads, and local bread
meals.dinner: Traditional Berber feast at the luxury desert camp — slow-cooked lamb mechoui, vegetable couscous, Moroccan salads, and fresh fruit, served under the stars with live Gnawa music around the campfire

day_by_day.notes: The drive from Marrakech to Merzouga is approximately 8–9 hours including stops — an early departure is essential. Ensure your luxury camp is pre-booked well in advance (recommended options: Scarabeo Camp, Luxury Desert Bivouac by Kasbah Tamadot, or similar 5-star glamping experience). Pack a warm layer — desert nights in March can drop to 5–10°C. Sunscreen and sunglasses are essential for the dune experience.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for a private sunrise hike or camel ride to the summit of the Erg Chebbi dunes — watching the Sahara ignite in shades of gold, pink, and crimson at sunrise is among Morocco's most transcendent experiences. Return to camp for a leisurely breakfast. Optional sandboarding session on the dunes with equipment provided by the camp.
day_by_day.afternoon: 4x4 desert excursion into the wider Erg Chebbi landscape — visit a traditional nomadic Berber family encampment for an authentic tea ceremony and cultural exchange. Explore the fossil-rich plateaus near Erfoud (Morocco is one of the world's richest sources of marine fossils). Visit a fossil artisan workshop to see craftsmen at work. Return to your camp or premium lodge for a relaxing afternoon with optional spa treatments.
day_by_day.evening: Private sundowner experience on a private dune with champagne or Moroccan tea service arranged by your camp. Second night under the stars — optional private astronomy session or simply relax by the campfire with traditional Berber music.

meals.breakfast: Full camp breakfast after sunrise — fresh fruit, Moroccan pastries, eggs prepared to order, yoghurt with local honey, and mint tea or coffee
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the camp or nomadic-style picnic in the desert — Moroccan salads, grilled meats, fresh bread, and seasonal fruit
meals.dinner: Elevated Berber-fusion dinner at camp — multi-course menu featuring slow-cooked lamb shoulder, saffron-spiced vegetable pastilla, and traditional desserts with rose water and orange blossom

day_by_day.notes: The pre-dawn wake-up is typically around 5:30–6:00 AM depending on the season — confirm exact sunrise time with your camp. Stay hydrated throughout the day as desert air is very dry. If you prefer a premium lodge over a camp, Kasbah Mohayut or Auberge Camping Yasmina offer luxury room options adjacent to the dunes.

day_by_day.morning: Depart the Sahara after breakfast and begin the scenic return journey toward Marrakech via an alternative southern route. Stop at the Todra Gorge — a spectacular canyon with 300-metre-high rose-pink limestone walls, one of Morocco's most dramatic natural landscapes. Short guided hike through the gorge floor along the river.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue through the Dadès Valley (Valley of a Thousand Kasbahs) — a cinematic landscape of crumbling earthen kasbahs, almond orchards, and rose fields. Stop at the Roses Valley (Vallée des Roses) near Kelâat M'Gouna — famous for its annual rose festival and fields of Rosa damascena. Visit a local rose cooperative to learn about distillation of rose water and argan-rose cosmetics. Continue driving toward Marrakech, arriving by early evening.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back at your Marrakech riad. Freshen up and enjoy a relaxed evening in the medina — a final wander through the illuminated Djemaa el-Fna square, souvenir shopping in the souks, or a quiet evening at the riad with a private rooftop dinner.

meals.breakfast: Final camp breakfast before departure — fresh Moroccan spread with pastries, eggs, fruit, and mint tea
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant near Todra Gorge — fresh trout from the gorge river (a local speciality), Moroccan salads, and traditional bread
meals.dinner: Dinner at Dar Cherifa — a beautifully restored 16th-century riad in the medina now operating as a cultural café and fine-dining space, offering refined Moroccan dishes in an intimate literary atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: The return drive from Merzouga to Marrakech via Todra Gorge is approximately 9–10 hours including stops — depart by 7:30–8:00 AM to arrive comfortably in the evening. The Roses Valley is at its most spectacular during the rose harvest (late April–May) but the valley and cooperative are worth visiting year-round. Consider purchasing premium rose water or argan-rose cosmetics directly from the cooperative.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Marrakech — visit the Ben Youssef Madrasa, a stunning 14th-century Islamic college considered the finest example of Moroccan-Andalusian architecture in the country, featuring exquisite carved stucco, zellige mosaic floors, and a serene marble courtyard. Continue to the Museum of Marrakech (Musée de Marrakech) housed in a palatial 19th-century mansion for a curated collection of Moroccan art and photography.
day_by_day.afternoon: Leisure time for last-minute premium souvenir shopping — visit specialist artisan workshops for hand-stamped leather goods, handwoven Berber carpets, silver jewellery, and high-quality argan oil products. Optional: private cooking class at a medina cooking school (La Maison Arabe Cookery School) to learn the secrets of Moroccan tagine and pastilla before departing.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at one of Marrakech's finest establishments. Private transfer to Marrakech Menara Airport for your departure flight.

meals.breakfast: Grand farewell breakfast at the riad — a full spread of all Moroccan breakfast classics enjoyed at a leisurely pace on the rooftop terrace with views of the medina
meals.lunch: Lunch at Pepe Nero — an elegant Moroccan-Italian fusion restaurant in a beautifully restored riad near the medina, offering refined dishes in a tranquil courtyard
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Le Jardin Secret Restaurant or Royal Mansour's La Grande Table Marocaine — the ultimate luxury Moroccan fine-dining experience with impeccable service, a curated wine and juice pairing menu, and a breathtaking palace setting

day_by_day.notes: Confirm departure flight time and arrange private airport transfer through your riad concierge. Allow at least 2.5–3 hours before departure for transfer and check-in. The Ben Youssef Madrasa is one of Marrakech's most visited sites — arrive early (opening time around 9:00 AM) to avoid crowds. Ensure any carpets or large purchases are properly documented for customs if required. La Grande Table Marocaine at Royal Mansour requires a reservation well in advance and is considered one of the finest dining experiences in all of Africa.
